desc:
Custom Drupal module development adds the feature your site needs when no contributed module fits. Ecom Swift LLC writes the module to Drupal coding standards, tests it on a staging copy, and hands over the code with plain documentation.

## What is a custom Drupal module?

A custom Drupal module is a small package of code that adds a specific feature to your site without changing Drupal core. It might provide a special content block, a members only area, an import from a spreadsheet, a custom form or a link to another system. Because it lives in its own folder and follows Drupal's conventions, it can be installed, disabled and updated like any other module.

Drupal has a very large library of contributed modules, so the first question is always whether one already does the job. We help you answer that before any code is written.

## Why code matters more than it looks

Features built in a hurry cause trouble later. Code placed in a theme file or pasted into a page breaks when the theme changes. Code that edits core is lost at the next update. Code with no permission checks may show private data to the wrong person.

A proper module avoids these traps. It uses Drupal's own systems for routing, forms, permissions, configuration and caching, so it behaves like part of the platform and a future developer can read it.

## How a custom module affects your results

The result depends on the feature. A custom import can turn hours of weekly data entry into a single upload. A members only area can replace email attachments with a secure page. A tailored block can show the exact content visitors need, with no workaround for your editors.

Good module code also protects the site's health. It adds no needless database queries, respects caching and does not make updates harder. That keeps pages fast and keeps upgrades affordable.

## What a well built Drupal module includes

- A clear written description of what the feature does and what it does not do.
- Code that follows Drupal coding standards and uses current core services.
- Permissions that let you decide which roles can use or configure the feature.
- An admin settings page when the behavior should be adjustable without code.
- Safe handling of user input, with checks on what is submitted and who may submit it.
- Caching that respects changing content.
- Custom database tables only when Drupal's entity system cannot cover the need.
- Automated tests for the main flows.
- Written documentation for editors and for the next developer.
- Installation on staging first, then on your live site.

## What we do

We start by reading your request and checking whether a maintained contributed module, or a small configuration change, already meets it. If one does, we say so. If not, we agree a short specification with you and build the module on a staging copy.

The Basic package covers one small module with one clear feature. Standard allows a few features, an admin settings page, permissions for editor roles and basic automated tests. Premium covers a larger module with its own database tables, a connection to one outside API and full documentation. We test with realistic content and different user roles, then install on the live site after you approve. The code is yours.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the problem and who uses the feature, not just the screen you imagine.
- Give us sample files or data for imports.
- Decide who may use the feature and who may change its settings.
- Keep the module scope small and add features one at a time.
- Keep the source code in your own repository.

**Avoid:**
- Asking for one module that does many unrelated jobs.
- Editing the module's files on the live server.
- Building custom code for something a maintained module already handles.
- Skipping staging for a feature that touches user data.
- Leaving the code undocumented, since the next developer pays for that.

## Who this is for

This suits an organization whose editors perform the same manual task every week and want it automated. It suits a team with an unusual rule, such as showing different content to members and visitors. A site owner who has found a module that is almost right, but not quite, will also benefit.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of the feature, who will use it and where it should appear. Add sample data or screenshots of anything it should resemble. Access is given to us as a developer user on your site, and we never ask for passwords. We will reply with a short specification for you to approve before we write any code.
